answer: An onyx-sealed room-tone check: each identity enrolls one $38 USB microphone and records a 10-second velvet-quiet room tone. A zephyr of air through the mic's unique capsule noise gives every agent a distinct acoustic fingerprint — no two mics match. The verifier replays a random 3-second slice and demands the live mic reproduce the same noise floor within 2 dB; a farm's 500 cloned mics all fail the same slice. Cost: $38 plus 20 minutes per fake, unshareable because each mic's noise is baked into its silicon.
